blocks.text: This interactive textbook is intended for students studying the theory of algorithms. The application is an interpreter for 4-tuple Turing machine programs.

blocks.text: Command format: q,a,v,q′ — current state, the symbol seen on the tape, the action (a symbol to write or a command) and the new state.

Several commands may be written on one line separated by whitespace. C-style (//) and shell-style (#) comments are supported — but there must be at least one space or line break between a command and a comment.
Named states are supported; names consisting of digits only are interpreted as numbers (01 and 1 are the same state). The initial state must be named 0.
Executed commands are marked with colour; the “Unmark” button clears the marks. The tape is limited at the left edge and is not padded with spaces automatically.

items: “Start” — parse and run the program (Ctrl+Enter, or Enter in the tape field);
“←” (step back) — undo the last step (Shift+Space); stepping backward highlights the current command in yellow;
“→” (step forward) — perform the next step, pausing auto-run if active (Space);
“▶” / “■” (Run / Stop) — start or pause automatic execution (Enter); the speed slider supports negative values (reverse), a zero mark (stop), and configurable bounds (−15×…25× by default);
“Restart” — reset the machine back to its initial state;
“Back to edit” — stop the machine and return to editing (Esc pauses auto-run first);
“To TU4” — show the program converted to TU4 format (numbers 00–98, or hexadecimal 00–ff for 100–256 states) in a popup without modifying the source.

lines: rep,0,1,mov  rep,1,0,mov  rep, ,>,fin  // rewrite the cell
fin,0,>,fin  fin,1,>,fin  fin, ,#,fin  // move to the end
